tickets.title: Queue admission does not treat a wontfix blocker as satisfied
tickets.what: imp-daily-facts/02 (`Blocked by: ticket-store/01`) and ticket-store/04 were admitted while ticket-store/01 was wontfix and its replacement ticket-store/06 had not landed; leads flagged it three times on 2026-11-26. A blocker counts as satisfied only when it is done; a wontfix blocker blocks until a ticket that names it as superseded (or the blocker's own comment naming a replacement `feature/NN`) is done. A wontfix blocker with no replacement is reported in `hud_tickets ready` as a blocked reason the main session must fix by editing `blocked_by`, never silently ignored.

acceptance.text: Test: blocker wontfix with replacement not done → ticket not ready; replacement done → ready
Test: wontfix blocker without a replacement → not ready, `ready` shows the reason naming the blocker
Same rule for cross-feature blockers and inside a running queue's admission

tickets.title: Queue items can target another repository
tickets.what: herdr-fork tickets live in MyHUD's tracker but most change ~/projects/herdr-hud. A queue run started from MyHUD dispatched herdr-fork/30 into a MyHUD worktree; the worker edited herdr-hud's main checkout uncommitted, and the land failed with 'Source has no commits to land' (2026-11-27, run q7aba5d9564d1e161). Main had to commit and install by hand, and `hud_create` refuses a `brief_file` outside the target cwd. Add an optional ticket field `repo` (a registered project root, JSON and Markdown `**Repo:**`); queue admission dispatches that item with cwd = repo, isolation worktree there, the brief rendered from the ticket, and lands it with that repo's land block; the ticket record (done/landing) is still written in the tracker project. A ticket whose repo is not registered stays not-ready with that reason.

Test: unregistered repo → not ready, reason names it
Test: hud_create with ticket A/NN and cwd B renders the brief from A's tracker

tickets.title: A waiting land never fails on a land-queue lock timeout
tickets.what: 2026-11-27 ~05:05Z three queued lands failed at once with `waiting for f19e4dd6188b00f6e (gate step 3, 0 min): abstract lock timeout (land-queue)` (unattended/13 ff4d4ccd31d0208eb-2, imp-daily-facts/07 f2d9ff6f38e77f4f4, ticket-store/09 fc93b02fed181360a) while another land held the gate. src/mcp/land-runner.ts:127 takes `withAbstractLock('land-queue', …)` with the default 1000 ms timeout (src/utils/abstract-lock.ts:34). Waiting lands call it every lease poll in `acquire` (~251) and `train()` (~516) holds it across per-candidate `runLock` calls (now up to 10 s after 810a146a), so with several waiters a poll times out and the exception fails the land. Fix: a lock timeout inside the waiting loop is a retry, never a land failure; keep the train claim's critical section short (no nested waits that can exceed the waiters' timeout) or give land-queue a timeout above its longest holder. Main re-queued the three lands by hand.

acceptance.text: Test: four lands queued behind a gate, with a train claim holding land-queue longer than the default timeout, all keep waiting and none fails; they land in order after the gate
Test: a genuine land-queue holder crash still recovers (existing stale-lock behaviour unchanged)
TZ=UTC node tests/run-mjs.mjs 8 passes

tickets.title: Auto-dispatched flake jobs land by themselves
tickets.what: The flake collector (chores/01) promotes a full flake list and dispatches its imp automatically, but the settled job just sits in idle_grace until main calls hud_land: test-flakes/22 (ja1d6db839e689f0a) and test-flakes/23 (jb1845189b28cf985) on 2026-11-27 both waited for main. A promoted flake job is unattended work with fixed acceptance (each case passes 20 consecutive parallel runs, no weakened assertions): when it settles with a report and a commit, HUD starts its land through the project's land block itself and notifies main only on land failure. A report with Blockers or a scope assumption still goes to main instead of landing.

Test: a flake report with a Blockers line or scope assumption does not land and notifies main

tickets.title: A land waits for its repair worker's answered question instead of failing
tickets.what: 2026-11-27: land ff4d4ccd31d0208eb-3 failed the moment its repair worker j927cfddb5c6d5ef6 asked main a question (`failed: cherry-pick (repair 1): … needs the main session: q1`). Main answered within minutes, the worker finished the repair and committed, but the land was already terminal, so main had to start a new land (-4) by hand. Same pattern earlier with je97ca49a97171be5 and j7f534f864a751fa0. While a repair worker has an open question the land stays in a waiting step (`repair 1: waiting for main (q1)`), and continues with the gate when the worker settles with a commit; it fails only if the worker fails, is closed, or the question goes unanswered past the normal question timeout.

tickets.title: A headless sonic that answers in chat without hud_report keeps its answer
tickets.what: Twice on 2026-11-26/27 a luna sonic (pi, openai/gpt-6-luna) finished its lookup, wrote the full answer as its final assistant message and exited without calling hud_report (latest j95360f77506837ee, child of reviewer j37c5c8f52507c874). HUD failed the job with "pi exited without a declared report" and the parent lost a correct answer; main had to dig it out of stdout.jsonl. When a headless sonic settles (agent_settled, not aborted, exit 0) with no declared report but a non-empty final assistant text, HUD publishes that text as the report, marked `salvaged: final message without hud_report` in the digest and with the usual unverified-facts prefix for the parent. No nudge or extra turn is sent (cli-workers/09 rule). Aborted runs, provider errors and empty final text still fail as today.

tickets.title: A late answer to a question never fails a job that already reported
tickets.what: 2026-11-27: imp jf33687c6d908554c (pi tab, herdr-fork/32) asked q2 at 22:33, kept working, committed and published a valid report (q2 moot). Main's answer landed at 22:43:07; it was delivered as a new turn, the turn ended without a new report, and at 22:43:14 `src/harness/pi/worker/tab-lifecycle.ts` settled the job `failed: output missing, empty or unchanged`. hud_land then refused the job (state failed) and main had to land by hand. An answer that arrives after the worker published a report for the turn that asked must not turn a reported job into failed: either deliver it without starting a turn that needs a new report, or settle that turn as `settled` when the earlier declared report stands (answer recorded as moot).
